findings.title: slowapi default_limits are dead config - 21 routes have NO rate limit at all
findings.claim: `limiter` is registered only as `app.state.limiter` and `SlowAPIMiddleware` is never added, so the `default_limits=[DAILY_LIMIT, ANON_LIMIT]` configured at app/middleware/rate_limiter.py:29 apply to nothing and the 21 routes without an explicit `@limiter.limit(...)` decorator are entirely unthrottled.
findings.evidence: app/main.py:110 sets `app.state.limiter = limiter` and adds ErrorHandler/SecurityHeaders/RequestID middleware only - `grep -rn 'SlowAPIMiddleware' app/ tests/` returns zero hits. slowapi/middleware.py `SlowAPIMiddleware.dispatch` is the ONLY consumer of default limits (`_should_exempt` returns early for routes in `limiter._route_limits`, i.e. decorated ones). Verified by running a TestClient repro: an undecorated route under `default_limits=['2/minute']` returned 200 five times in a row; the decorated twin returned 429 on the third. Enumerated the 21 undecorated routes by script: auth_routes.py:548 POST /logout, :563 GET /me, :615 GET /verify, :628 PUT /profile, :638 PUT /email, :654 PUT /password, :711 GET /preferences, :758 PUT /preferences, :1018 GET /cohort-profile; text_routes.py:695 DELETE /cache, :730 GET /parse; url_routes.py:46 GET /retailers; usage_routes.py:9 GET /status; version_routes.py:19 GET /version; legal_routes.py:17,18,34,35; referral_routes.py:231 GET /status, :248 GET /invite/{share_token}, :275 POST /invite/{share_token}/quiz.
findings.failure_scenario: PUT /api/v1/auth/password (auth_routes.py:654) and PUT /api/v1/auth/email (:638) both take `current_password` and are verified against Supabase. With a stolen/borrowed access token (a shared device, a leaked token, an XSS in a webview) an attacker can submit unlimited `current_password` guesses at full network speed - there is no per-route limit, no default limit, and `check_account_locked` is only consulted on POST /login, never here. The same hole makes POST /api/v1/referrals/invite/{token}/quiz an unauthenticated, unbounded work amplifier.
findings.fix_sketch: Either `app.add_middleware(SlowAPIMiddleware)` in main.py so `default_limits` actually apply, or decorate the 21 routes individually. The credential-checking ones (PUT /email, PUT /password) need a tight explicit limit (e.g. 5/minute) plus the same `check_account_locked`/`track_failed_login` treatment POST /login gets.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-derived independently. (a) `grep -rn SlowAPIMiddleware . --include=*.py` -> ZERO hits; app/main.py:110 sets only `app.state.limiter = limiter`, and the middleware stack added at :123-129 is ErrorHandler/SecurityHeaders/RequestID only. `ls app/middleware/` shows no other throttle, and security.py/request_id.py contain no 429 path. (b) Read the INSTALLED slowapi 0.1.10: middleware.py's SlowAPIMiddleware.dispatch is the only caller of `_check_request_limit(..., in_middleware=True)`, and extension.py:611-629 only reaches `all_limits += list(itertools.chain(*self._default_limits))` when `combined_defaults` holds, which a decorated route (override_defaults=True) never satisfies. (c) RAN my own zero-network repro (scratchpad/m13/security/verify/repro_slowapi.py): default_limits=['2/minute'] -> undecorated route [200,200,200,200,200]; decorated twin [200,200,429,429,429]. (d) Re-enumerated with my own scanner: 78 @router.<verb> registrations, 21 with no @limiter.limit between decorator and def -- an EXACT match for the lane's list, file and line, including auth_routes.py:638 PUT /email and :654 PUT /password. (e) `grep -rn 'check_account_locked|track_failed_login' app/` returns hits ONLY at auth_routes.py:459/:483 inside POST /login, so the credential-checking PUT /email and PUT /password have neither a rate limit nor the lockout counter. Corroboration the lane missed: tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py is docstringed 'verifying rate limiting on all public endpoints' / 'Verify every public endpoint has rate limiting configured', and its 16 tests touch NONE of the 21 -- that green is what makes this invisible.

findings.title: Rate-limit key and audit ip_address are the Railway edge-proxy IP, not the client
findings.claim: `get_remote_address` returns `request.client.host` (the immediate TCP peer) and nothing in the repo enables or trusts proxy headers, so behind Railway's edge every request shares ONE rate-limit bucket and every `admin_audit_log.ip_address` row records the proxy, not the actor.
findings.evidence: app/middleware/rate_limiter.py:26-30 builds `Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address, storage_uri='memory://')`; slowapi's `get_remote_address` is literally `return request.client.host` (inspected in the installed package) - it never reads `X-Forwarded-For`. `grep -rni 'x-forwarded|forwarded_allow|proxy-headers|proxy_headers|cf-connecting' app/ scripts/ Procfile railway.json .github/` returns ZERO hits. Procfile:1 and railway.json `startCommand` are both bare `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`, and uvicorn's ProxyHeadersMiddleware only rewrites `client` for peers in `--forwarded-allow-ips` (default 127.0.0.1), which Railway's edge is not. The only consumers of a real client IP are auth_routes.py:437,465,488,506 which pass `request.client.host` as `ip_address` into `log_audit_event`.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concrete consequences. (a) Availability: POST /auth/login is `5/minute` - if all callers hash to one key, five failed logins anywhere in the world lock the login endpoint for every user for the rest of that minute, and 10/minute on /text/compare caps the entire product at 10 comparisons/minute. (b) Forensics: the `brute_force_lockout` / `login_failed` audit rows that `admin_routes.py:194 /audit-log` exists to serve all carry the same proxy IP, so the abuse-investigation surface built in Bundle A/D cannot attribute anything.
findings.fix_sketch: Run uvicorn with `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'` (safe only because Railway terminates at its own edge), or supply a `key_func` that reads the left-most untrusted-but-useful `X-Forwarded-For` entry, and use the same helper for the `ip_address` audit field. Add a test asserting two requests with different XFF get different limiter keys.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-derived. I ran the absence grep myself: `grep -rniE 'x-forwarded|forwarded_allow|proxy-headers|proxy_headers|cf-connecting|X-Real-IP' app/ scripts/ Procfile railway.json .github/` -> ZERO hits. Procfile:1 is `web: uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` and railway.json deploy.startCommand is byte-identical -- no --proxy-headers, no --forwarded-allow-ips. app/middleware/rate_limiter.py:26-30 is `Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address, storage_uri='memory://', default_limits=[DAILY_LIMIT, ANON_LIMIT])`; I printed slowapi's installed get_remote_address source -- it is exactly `return request.client.host` with a 127.0.0.1 fallback and never reads a header. I also inspected the installed uvicorn 0.30.0 ProxyHeadersMiddleware: it IS installed by default, but trusted_hosts defaults to '127.0.0.1' and it rewrites scope['client'] only when the TCP peer is in that set. Railway's edge is not 127.0.0.1 to the container, so scope['client'] stays the proxy. Audit consumers confirmed at auth_routes.py:437/:465/:488/:506 (`request.client.host if request.client else None`). Residual uncertainty, stated honestly and not changing the verdict: the cardinality of Railway's edge peers is unobservable from a read-only tree, so 'ONE bucket' may in practice be 'a handful'. Either way the key is not the client, so both consequences -- shared throttle and unattributable admin_audit_log.ip_address -- hold. P1 kept.

findings.title: GET /api/v1/auth/verify returns the caller's JWT in the response body, breaking the invariant recorded in auth_service
findings.claim: `verify_auth` returns `"user": current_user` wholesale, and `verify_token` puts the raw `access_token` into that dict, so every /auth/verify response echoes a live Supabase JWT into a response body - the exact dict the code comments forbid handling loosely.
findings.evidence: app/api/auth_routes.py:615-625: `@router.get('/verify')` -> `return {'success': True, 'valid': True, 'user': current_user}`. app/services/auth_service.py:255-260 returns `{'id':..., 'email':..., 'access_token': access_token}`. The docstring at auth_service.py:239-243 states verbatim: 'Security note: do NOT log the full `current_user` dict at any call site (it now contains a secret). Existing log statements use only `current_user['id']` - verified safe at audit time.' The audit that added `access_token` (H4, 2026-05-22) checked log statements but not response bodies. Every other endpoint that returns a user (GET /me, :570-581) builds an explicit whitelist dict; /verify is the one that does not.
findings.failure_scenario: A user calls /auth/verify on app start (CLAUDE.md: 'Useful for checking auth status on app startup'). The JWT now appears in: the mobile client's own response logging, any APM/response-capture, Sentry's Starlette integration if the request later errors (response bodies are not covered by `_before_send`'s header/query scrubbing), and any intermediary that logs bodies. A token that should exist only in expo-secure-store and the Authorization header is duplicated into a payload nobody treats as secret.
findings.fix_sketch: Return an explicit whitelist, mirroring GET /me: `{'success': True, 'valid': True, 'user': {'id': current_user['id'], 'email': current_user.get('email')}}`. Add a regression test asserting `'access_token' not in json.dumps(response.json())` for /verify (and sweep every route that returns a `current_user`-derived object).
findings.verify_evidence: Facts fully reproduced; severity overstated. app/api/auth_routes.py:615-625 is verbatim `@router.get('/verify')` -> `return {'success': True, 'valid': True, 'user': current_user}`; app/services/auth_service.py:255-259 returns `{'id':..., 'email':..., 'access_token': access_token}`; the docstring at auth_service.py:239-243 does say 'do NOT log the full current_user dict at any call site (it now contains a secret)'. I ran my own grep for return sites across app/api/*.py: auth_routes.py:624 is the ONLY route returning the dict wholesale (GET /me at :563-597 builds an explicit whitelist), so the lane's absence claim holds. DOWNGRADE reason: the JWT is echoed ONLY to the caller who just presented that same JWT in the Authorization header -- no cross-principal disclosure. Every consequence in the failure scenario requires a SECOND independent flaw (a client that logs response bodies, an APM capture, a body-logging intermediary). I read sentry_service.py:128-175 `_before_send`: it scrubs exception values, breadcrumbs, request headers and the request URL, and never touches response bodies, so Sentry is not a carrier either way. Real invariant violation, cheap fix, but not P1.

findings.title: Magento GraphQL adapter POSTs to a URL taken verbatim from a remote configs.json (unvalidated SSRF sink)
findings.claim: Shape-A resolution fetches `https://{host}/configs.json`, reads `commerce-endpoint` out of the remote JSON with no scheme/host/IP validation, caches it for 24h, and then POSTs the GraphQL query - plus the harvested `x-api-key` header - to whatever URL that remote document named.
findings.evidence: app/services/magento_graphql_service.py:428-445 `_harvest_shape_a_config` GETs `f'https://{host}/configs.json'`. :391-425 `_parse_configs` does `endpoint = flat.get('commerce-endpoint')` and returns it in the cfg dict with no validation beyond a truthiness check at :414. :1027-1042 builds the header dict (`x-api-key`, `Magento-*`) and calls `_post_graphql(cfg['endpoint'], _SHAPE_A_QUERY, {...}, headers)`. :507-527 `_post_graphql` calls `curl_requests.post(url, ..., allow_redirects=True)` directly. `grep -rn 'validate_external_url' app/services/magento_graphql_service.py` returns ZERO hits - the SSRF validator is imported by url_routes, price_service, shopify_pdp_service and url_extraction_service, never here.
findings.failure_scenario: A registry host in `_MAGENTO_STORES` is compromised (or a hostile operator publishes a poisoned config) and serves `{"data":[{"key":"commerce-endpoint","value":"http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"}, ...]}`. Every subsequent Shape-A price lookup for 24h POSTs from inside the Railway container to that address, carrying our request headers, and the response body is JSON-parsed and fed into the price cascade. `http://<service>.railway.internal:<port>/` works the same way. Gated by `ENABLE_MAGENTO_GQL_ADAPTER` (default OFF), which is why this is latent rather than live - it is on the activation runbook's step (1).
findings.fix_sketch: Before caching a harvested cfg, require `urlparse(endpoint).scheme in ('https',)` AND `_host_on_domain(endpoint, host)` (or an explicit per-store allowlist of endpoint hosts, since Alshaya endpoints are stable), AND `validate_external_url(endpoint)`. Same treatment for `base_endpoint` and for the jomashop persisted-query endpoint at :469-495. Pin it with a test that a poisoned configs.json yields None, not a POST.
findings.verify_evidence: Code facts reproduced exactly. app/services/magento_graphql_service.py:428-445 `_harvest_shape_a_config` GETs `f'https://{host}/configs.json'` with allow_redirects=True; :391-425 `_parse_configs` pulls `endpoint = flat.get('commerce-endpoint')` and the only gate is the truthiness check at :414 (`if not (endpoint and env_id and api_key and store_view and website and store_code): return None`) -- no scheme, host or IP check; :1024-1042 builds the x-api-key / Magento-* header dict from the harvested cfg and calls `_post_graphql(cfg['endpoint'], ...)`; :511-527 `_post_graphql` calls `curl_requests.post(url, ..., allow_redirects=True)` with no validation. I ran `grep -c validate_external_url app/services/magento_graphql_service.py` -> 0. Every element of the claim is true. DOWNGRADE reason: exploitation needs TWO preconditions, both currently false. (1) `magento_gql_adapter_enabled()` at :212 reads ENABLE_MAGENTO_GQL_ADAPTER, default OFF, and CLAUDE.md:332 lists it in the M5 ship-dark set with no record of a Railway flip. (2) The attacker must already control a `_MAGENTO_STORES` (:78) registry host's /configs.json -- an upstream compromise. That is the same shape as security-05, which this lane itself rated P2. Real defect that MUST be fixed before activation-runbook step (1), but not a live exposure.

findings.title: The Codex HIGH-5 SSRF hardening was never propagated to the M5-M12 adapters - 17 fetch sites follow redirects unvalidated
findings.claim: The price HTML path (`curl_fetch_html_same_site`) and the sitemap builder (`_default_fetch`) were explicitly hardened to validate the initial URL and EVERY redirect hop, but the newer adapters all call curl_cffi with `allow_redirects=True` and no per-hop check, so a 30x from any registry host walks the fetch off-domain and into private space.
findings.evidence: The hardened pattern is documented at app/services/price_service.py:13672-13700 ('Redirect-validating same-site HTML fetch (Codex HIGH-5 SSRF fix)') and re-stated at app/services/sitemap_discovery_service.py:699-717. The unhardened sites, all `allow_redirects=True` with no `validate_external_url` and no `_host_on_domain`: salla_service.py:98 (storefront GET `https://{domain}/`) and :217 (search API); magento_graphql_service.py:445, :491, :525, :654; occ_service.py:289; rest_json_service.py:268, :326, :411; yotpo_service.py:266; judgeme/algolia_service.py:246,:262; unbxd_service.py:197; woocommerce_service.py:294; noon_service.py:147; and price_service.py:13638 (`curl_fetch_html`, still live), :14022, :14065, :15039, :15101. `grep -rn 'validate_external_url' app/services/` shows the validator reaches only price_service, shopify_pdp_service, url_extraction_service and sitemap_discovery_service.
findings.failure_scenario: reefperfumes.com (a live Salla registry row) is compromised and its root responds `302 Location: http://10.x.x.x:8000/admin/`. `_resolve_store_id` (salla_service.py:88-108) follows it and hands the internal response body to `_extract_store_id`. For price_service.py:13638 `curl_fetch_html`, the URL is not even registry-pinned: structured_comparison_service.py:2321 feeds it a link taken from a Serper organic result, so the fetch target is influenced by the user's own query text.
findings.fix_sketch: Give the adapters the same helper: a shared `fetch_json_same_site(url, domain)` that mirrors `curl_fetch_html_same_site` (allow_redirects=False, per-hop `validate_external_url` + `_host_on_domain`, hop cap, body cap). Retire the bare `curl_fetch_html` or route its two remaining callers through the same-site variant bound to the URL's own registrable domain.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-derived with my own greps, not the lane's. `grep -rln validate_external_url app/` returns only app/api/url_routes.py, app/services/price_service.py, app/services/shopify_pdp_service.py, app/services/sitemap_discovery_service.py, app/services/url_extraction_service.py and the validator itself -- the M5-M12 adapters are absent, as claimed. `grep -rn 'allow_redirects=True' app/services/*.py` gives 23 sites across 11 modules (price_service 6, magento_graphql 4, rest_json 3, salla 2, algolia 2, yotpo/woocommerce/unbxd/sitemap_discovery/occ/noon 1 each). Spot-verified four cited lines by opening them: salla_service.py:88-108 `_resolve_store_id` GETs `https://{domain}/` with allow_redirects=True and hands resp.text to `_extract_store_id`; occ_service.py:283-292 and yotpo_service.py:260-268 are the same shape. Verified the CONTRAST is real, not invented: price_service.py:13672-13700 `curl_fetch_html_same_site` carries the 'Codex HIGH-5 SSRF fix' docstring and validates the initial URL via validate_external_url + _host_on_domain, and sitemap_discovery_service.py:697-717 `_default_fetch` routes through it under an explicit SSRF-GUARD comment. Verified the strongest sub-claim myself: price_service.py:13631 `curl_fetch_html` is still live, and structured_comparison_service.py:2321 feeds it `sp`, a link taken from a Serper organic result filtered only by the substring test `bd in (link or '').lower()` at :2312. P2 correct: exploitation still needs a compromised registry host or a poisoned index entry.

findings.title: /openapi.json is still public in production - only the docs UIs were disabled
findings.claim: `docs_url` and `redoc_url` are set to None under `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT`, but `openapi_url` is left at its FastAPI default, so the complete machine-readable API schema - every admin route, every parameter, every model - is served unauthenticated at /openapi.json in prod.
findings.evidence: app/main.py:79-80: `docs_url=None if os.getenv('RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT') else '/docs'`, `redoc_url=...` - no `openapi_url` argument. Verified against the installed fastapi 0.115.0: `FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None).routes` -> `['/openapi.json']`. CLAUDE.md's security section claims '**Swagger** disabled in prod' and the App-Store routine treats that as done.
findings.failure_scenario: `curl https://web-production-58776.up.railway.app/openapi.json` returns the full contract including the 19 `/api/v1/admin/*` endpoints, the `X-Admin-Key` header name, the `/api/v1/text/cache` DELETE and `/api/v1/text/parse` debug routes, and every request-model field name and constraint - handing an attacker the exact enumeration this review had to derive by reading source.
findings.fix_sketch: `openapi_url=None if os.getenv('RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT') else '/openapi.json'` on the FastAPI constructor. Add a test that asserts a 404 on /openapi.json when RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT is set.
findings.verify_evidence: app/main.py:79-80 read directly: `docs_url=None if os.getenv('RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT') else '/docs'`, `redoc_url=None if ... else '/redoc'` -- and there is no `openapi_url` argument anywhere in the FastAPI(...) constructor at lines 56-81. RAN the check against the installed fastapi 0.115.0: `FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None).routes` -> `['/openapi.json']`. The schema route survives both disables. Status-claim check: CLAUDE.md:224 does say '**Swagger** disabled in prod', which is the half-truth the finding names. The /api/v1/admin/* enumeration, the X-Admin-Key header name and the DELETE /api/v1/text/cache + GET /api/v1/text/parse debug routes are all in that schema. P2 correct -- information disclosure, no direct compromise.

findings.title: The last 10 characters of OPENAI_API_KEY are written to logs at INFO on every cold client init
findings.claim: `get_client()` logs `f'Initializing OpenAI client with key ending in: ...{api_key[-10:]}'` at INFO level, putting a 10-character slice of a live credential into Railway logs and any log sink downstream.
findings.evidence: app/services/extraction_service.py:41-51: the lazy initializer reads `os.getenv('OPENAI_API_KEY')` then `logger.info(f'Initializing OpenAI client with key ending in: ...{api_key[-10:] if api_key else "NONE"}')` BEFORE constructing `AsyncOpenAI`. logging_config.py routes this to structured JSON on stdout, which Railway retains. Nothing redacts it: the Sentry scrubbers in sentry_service.py only run on Sentry events, not on stdout.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone with Railway log access (or a future log-shipping integration, or a support screenshot) gets a 10-char suffix of the production OpenAI key. That is a meaningful head start on a partially-leaked key and it materially weakens the key-rotation posture CLAUDE.md documents elsewhere ('Full keys ONLY in gitignored .env'). It fires on every process cold start.
findings.fix_sketch: Log presence and length only - `logger.info('OpenAI client initialized (key present=%s, len=%d)', bool(api_key), len(api_key or ''))` - or drop the line entirely; the `[models] ...` startup line already identifies the deployment.
findings.verify_evidence: app/services/extraction_service.py:45 verbatim (I grepped for the exact string, the lane's line number is right): `logger.info(f"Initializing OpenAI client with key ending in: ...{api_key[-10:] if api_key else 'NONE'}")`, sitting between the `os.getenv('OPENAI_API_KEY')` read at :42 and the `AsyncOpenAI(...)` construction at :46. It is INFO, not DEBUG, so it survives the default LOG_LEVEL='INFO' configured at main.py:15. Confirmed nothing redacts stdout: sentry_service.py's scrubbers run only inside `_before_send` on Sentry events (I read :128-175); there is no logging filter on this path. `get_client()` is the lazy initializer for the core extraction path, so this fires on every process cold start. P2 correct: a 10-char suffix is a partial credential leak, not a usable key.

findings.title: Sentry's OpenAI-key scrubber only matches sk-proj- keys; classic sk- and sk-svcacct- keys pass through unredacted
findings.claim: `_SENSITIVE_PATTERNS` matches `sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` specifically, and no other pattern in the list can catch a non-project OpenAI key, so any key not in the `sk-proj-` format reaches Sentry in exception strings and breadcrumb messages verbatim.
findings.evidence: app/services/sentry_service.py:15-21 - the five patterns are a JWT triple-segment regex, `sk-proj-...`, `fc-[a-f0-9]{20,}`, `[a-f0-9]{32,}` (lowercase hex only), and `Bearer\s+...`. A classic `sk-<48 mixed-case base62>` or `sk-svcacct-...` key matches none of them: it is not `sk-proj-`, it is not all-lowercase-hex, and it is not preceded by `Bearer` when it appears inside an OpenAI SDK error string. `_scrub_string` (:93-97) applies only that list; the key-name denylist at :90 only helps for dict-valued fields, not for free text.
findings.failure_scenario: An OpenAI SDK error (`AuthenticationError`, a 401 body echo, or a `str(e)` from openai_service) that embeds the key hits `capture_exception` in ErrorHandlerMiddleware (error_handler.py:152-154). `_before_send` scrubs `exception.values[].value` through `_scrub_string`, which leaves the key intact, and it is stored in Sentry. Note the repo's own comment at sentry_service.py:9-14 says the pattern list is 'defense-in-depth against future provider keys' - this is the gap it was meant to close.
findings.fix_sketch: Broaden to `sk-(proj-|svcacct-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}` and add the shapes the repo actually uses that are currently uncovered: Upstash REST tokens, `GOCSPX-`, Railway/EAS tokens. Pin each with a test in tests/ that feeds a fake key of each shape through `_scrub_string`.
findings.verify_evidence: The regex gap is REAL and I proved it by running the repo's own scrubber. Fed five shapes through `app.services.sentry_service._scrub_string`: classic `sk-Ab3XmQz7...` -> returned UNCHANGED; `sk-svcacct-...` -> UNCHANGED; `GOCSPX-...` -> UNCHANGED; an Upstash-style token -> UNCHANGED; only `sk-proj-...` -> '[OPENAI_KEY_REDACTED]'. sentry_service.py:15-20's five patterns behave exactly as claimed, and `_scrub_string` (:93-97) applies only that list. DOWNGRADE reason: I could not find a CARRIER in this tree. `grep -rnE 'token=\{|api_key=\{|\?token='` over app/services/*.py finds no site that interpolates a live key into a string reachable by capture_exception, and `_before_send` scrubs only exception values, breadcrumbs and request headers. A defence-in-depth pattern gap with no demonstrated path to an actual leak is P3, not P2.

findings.title: The pre-commit credential guard misses the repo's highest-value secret shapes, including the Supabase service-role JWT
findings.claim: The staged-diff secrets grep covers only `sk-`, `AKIA`, `xox[baprs]-` and PEM private keys - it does not cover `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` (an `eyJ...` JWT that bypasses RLS on every user table), the Serper/Scrape.do/Zyte hex keys, `fc-` Firecrawl keys, Upstash REST tokens, or `GOCSPX-` Google client secrets.
findings.evidence: .githooks/pre-commit:47-59 - the guard is `grep -qE '(\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}|-----BEGIN (RSA |EC |OPENSSH )?PRIVATE KEY-----)'`. Every credential named in CLAUDE.md's 'Environment Variables (Railway) -> Required' block except OPENAI_API_KEY falls outside that set. findings.title: Search-descriptor url_template is never host- or scheme-checked, and it is derived from remote homepage HTML
findings.claim: `format_search_url` substitutes `{q}` into a stored `url_template` after checking only kind/robots_allowed/'{q}' presence - there is no check that the template's host belongs to the registry row it is keyed on - while `search_form_template` builds that template by `urljoin`-ing a search-`<form action>` read out of the store's own homepage, so remote content decides where the resulting URL points.
findings.evidence: app/services/search_descriptor_service.py:132-143 `usable` checks `kind in ('platform_api','onsite_html')`, `robots_allowed`, and `'{q}' in url_template` - nothing about the host. :228-238 `format_search_url` then does `descriptor.url_template.replace('{q}', quote_plus(q))`. :380-389 `search_form_template` does `url = urljoin(base_url, action or '/')` and accepts it as long as `parsed.scheme and parsed.netloc` - an absolute `action="https://third-party.example/s"` passes. scripts/resolve_search_descriptors.py:232-239 persists whatever `probe_search_descriptor` returned with no host assertion. The consumer is app/services/price_service.py:9091-9142 `_descriptor_search_url` -> `build_retailer_url`, whose output is surfaced as `price.url` / `rating_source.url` and opened by the app's `openRatingSource()`. I audited the shipped store (data/search_descriptors.json, 95 hosts: 43 platform_api, 42 sitemap, 6 none, 4 onsite_html) and confirmed 0 off-host templates today - so this is an unenforced invariant, not a live break.
findings.failure_scenario: Third-party hosted search is common (Searchanise, Algolia proxies), so a legitimate re-run of `resolve_search_descriptors.py --live` can persist an off-host template without anyone noticing; a compromised or hostile storefront can do it deliberately by serving `<form role=search action="https://attacker.tld/collect">`. With `ENABLE_SEARCH_DESCRIPTOR=true` (already SEEDED per CLAUDE.md, runbook step 6 is 'a pure flag-flip'), `build_retailer_url` then hands users an attacker-controlled link labelled as the retailer, and the same URL is a server-side fetch target for any caller that fetches what build_retailer_url returns. `http://169.254.169.254/?q=` also satisfies the scheme+netloc test.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a host assertion to `SearchDescriptor.usable` (or, better, at parse time in `parse_search_descriptor`): the template's `urlparse().hostname` must equal or be a subdomain of the registry row's domain, and the scheme must be https. Reject at resolution time in `search_form_template` too, so an off-host action is recorded as `kind='none'` rather than persisted. Pin with a test that a template pointing at another host is not `usable`.
findings.verify_evidence: Opened all three sites. search_descriptor_service.py:132-143 `usable` is exactly `self.kind in ('platform_api','onsite_html') and bool(self.robots_allowed) and '{q}' in (self.url_template or '')` -- no host, no scheme. :228-238 `format_search_url` is a bare `descriptor.url_template.replace('{q}', quote_plus(q))` behind that same gate. :380-389 `search_form_template` does `url = urljoin(base_url, action or '/')` and accepts it on `if not parsed.scheme or not parsed.netloc: return None`, so an absolute off-host `action=` passes and so does `http://169.254.169.254/?q={q}`. I INDEPENDENTLY re-audited the shipped store rather than trusting the lane's number: my own script over data/search_descriptors.json reports 95 hosts, kinds {platform_api: 43, sitemap: 42, none: 6, onsite_html: 4}, and 0 templates whose hostname is off the row's own host -- an exact match. So this is an unenforced invariant that currently holds, not a live break. P2 correct.

findings.title: Paid-work endpoints are unauthenticated and outside the freemium gate; the 'internal' KPI endpoint has the loosest limit of all
findings.claim: The usage gate is applied only `if user and user.get('id')`, so anonymous callers get unmetered OpenAI+Serper work on /text/compare, /text/compare/stream, /text/quick, /text/prices/{product}, /text/price-kpi and /image/identify - and /text/price-kpi, documented as an 'Internal/measurement surface', is unauthenticated at 30/minute, three times the limit of /compare.
findings.evidence: app/api/text_routes.py:155-157 `if user and user.get('id'): usage_check = await check_usage_allowed(...)` - the anonymous branch does nothing (same shape at :303 and :440). :636-692 `price_kpi` is `@limiter.limit('30/minute')` with NO auth dependency and calls `parse_product_query(q)` (an OpenAI chat completion, extraction_service.py:1302) plus `service._get_price(...)` (the full Serper price cascade). :562-592 `quick_compare` has no auth dependency and no usage check at all. :595-633 `get_gcc_prices` is 20/minute, no auth. app/api/image_routes.py:57-65 `identify_and_compare` takes `get_optional_user` and never calls `check_usage_allowed`, then runs GPT-4o-mini vision + a full comparison. `grep check_usage_allowed app/api/` shows the gate exists ONLY in text_routes.
findings.failure_scenario: An unauthenticated script hitting `GET /api/v1/text/price-kpi?q=<random>&nocache=true` runs one OpenAI parse plus the escalation-heavy price cascade per call (CLAUDE.md: '~10-15 [Serper] credits each post-B.0'). At 30/min that is ~450 Serper credits and 30 OpenAI calls per minute from one caller with no account - and because `SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT` ships UNSET the spend gate is INERT (CLAUDE.md, Serper spend controls), so nothing stops it before the key is drained. The freemium tier this project sells (3 lifetime / 10 per month) is bypassed simply by not sending an Authorization header.
findings.fix_sketch: Put /text/price-kpi behind `Depends(verify_admin_key)` like its sibling debug routes /text/cache and /text/parse. For the public compare surfaces, extend the usage gate to anonymous callers keyed on `X-Device-Fingerprint` (the header already exists and is regex-validated at auth_routes.py:22/366) or require auth. Add the gate to /image/identify and /text/quick.
findings.verify_evidence: Every fact reproduced, and the severity is understated. text_routes.py:155-157, :302-304 and :439-441 are all `if user and user.get('id'): usage_check = await check_usage_allowed(...)` -- the anonymous branch is empty. I ran `grep -rn check_usage_allowed app/ --include=*.py` myself: it appears ONLY at text_routes.py:22/158/303/440 and inside usage_service.py. image_routes.py:57-65 `identify_and_compare` takes Depends(get_optional_user) and never calls it. text_routes.py:562-563 `/quick` is `@limiter.limit('10/minute')` with no auth dependency and no usage check at all. text_routes.py:636-637 `/price-kpi` is `@limiter.limit('30/minute')` with NO auth dependency (I read the full signature at :638-641), and its body calls `parse_product_query(q)` -- a real OpenAI chat completion at extraction_service.py:1302-1322 -- plus `service._get_price(...)`, the full Serper cascade. Its own docstring calls it an 'Internal/measurement surface'. Its sibling debug route DELETE /cache at :695-699 DOES carry Depends(verify_admin_key), so the omission is an outlier rather than a house pattern. UPGRADE reason: unlike every other finding in this lane it needs NO precondition -- no feature flag, no upstream compromise, no stolen token. An anonymous caller spends the project's paid OpenAI and Serper credits, and CLAUDE.md:326 states in bold that SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT ships UNSET and 'unset means the spend gate is INERT'. findings.title: POST /text/compare body fields carry no max_length, unlike their GET twins
findings.claim: `TextCompareRequest.query`, `.product_a`, `.product_b`, `.region` and `.selected_category` are bare `Optional[str]`/`str` with no `Field(max_length=...)`, while the GET variants of the same parameters are capped at 500 / 80 / 20 - so the POST path accepts an unbounded string where the GET path rejects it.
findings.evidence: app/api/text_routes.py:46-53 - `query: Optional[str] = None`, `product_a: Optional[str] = None`, `product_b: Optional[str] = None`, `region: str = 'bahrain'`, `selected_category: Optional[str] = None`. Contrast :246-249 (GET /compare) `q: Optional[str] = Query(None, max_length=500)`, `product_a: ... max_length=80`, and :641 `region: str = Query('bahrain', max_length=20)`. Same gap on `QuickCompareRequest` at :69-73 (`product1: str`, `product2: str`, no caps). Downstream, `parse_product_query` truncates at 500 (extraction_service.py:1312) but `structured_comparison_service` passes `explicit_pair` values through a separate path sanitized at only 80 (:3009, :3501), and the raw string is logged in full at text_routes.py:137 and written to `search_logs.query`.
findings.failure_scenario: `POST /api/v1/text/compare` with a 5 MB `query` value: the string is logged in full at :137 (`logger.info(f'Text comparison request: {body.query}')`), written to `search_logs` by `log_search`, and carried through the orchestrator. FastAPI applies no default body-size limit, so this is an unauthenticated log-flood / row-bloat primitive, and the asymmetry means a validation fix applied to the GET route gives false confidence about the POST one.
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror the GET constraints on the model: `query: Optional[str] = Field(None, max_length=500)`, `product_a/product_b: Optional[str] = Field(None, max_length=80)`, `region: str = Field('bahrain', max_length=20)`, `selected_category: Optional[str] = Field(None, max_length=32)`, and the same on `QuickCompareRequest`. Truncate or hash the query in the :137 log line.
findings.verify_evidence: text_routes.py:45-52 read verbatim: `query: Optional[str] = None`, `product_a: Optional[str] = None`, `product_b: Optional[str] = None`, `region: str = 'bahrain'`, `selected_category: Optional[str] = None` -- no Field(max_length=...) on any, and the `normalize_shape` model_validator at :54-65 checks only the either/or shape, never length. `QuickCompareRequest` at :68-72 is `product1: str` / `product2: str`, also uncapped. The asymmetry is real: the GET twin at :247-249 is `q: ... Query(None, max_length=500)` and `product_a/product_b: ... max_length=80`, and price-kpi at :640-641 caps q at 200 and region at 20. Nit on the lane's evidence: GET /compare's own `region` at :252 is ALSO uncapped -- the max_length=20 it cites belongs to price-kpi, not to the GET /compare twin. text_routes.py:137 `logger.info(f'Text comparison request: {body.query}')` logs the full untruncated value. Bounding fact the lane omitted: POST /compare IS decorated `@limiter.limit('10/minute')` at :121, so the flood is throttled per key -- which is why P2 rather than higher. The core claim (a validation asymmetry that makes a GET-side fix look complete) is airtight.

findings.title: Raw exception text is returned to the client on the camera comparison path
findings.claim: `identify_and_compare` catches every exception from the comparison and returns `{'error': str(e), ...}` at HTTP 200, bypassing the unified error envelope that exists precisely to keep internal detail out of responses.
findings.evidence: app/api/image_routes.py:247-271 - `except Exception as e:` then `return {'success': False, 'action': 'comparison_failed', 'error': str(e), 'products': products, ...}`. Compare app/middleware/error_handler.py:131-162 `ErrorHandlerMiddleware`, which deliberately replaces any unhandled exception with the constant string 'Internal server error'. The route is `get_optional_user`, so an anonymous caller receives this. The same `str(e)` is also written to `search_logs.error_message` at :258, which is fine.
findings.failure_scenario: A Supabase/httpx/asyncpg failure inside `compare_from_text` surfaces its message to an anonymous HTTP client - these messages routinely embed hostnames, table names, row counts, Postgres error codes, and upstream URLs. An attacker uploads two images repeatedly and reads the differences in exception text to map the backend, which is exactly the reconnaissance the unified envelope was introduced to prevent.
findings.fix_sketch: Return a constant user-facing message plus the `request_id` (already on `request.state.request_id`) and keep `str(e)` in the log/Sentry path only, matching `_surface_comparison_failure` in text_routes.py:89-112.
findings.verify_evidence: app/api/image_routes.py:246-271: `except Exception as e:` ... `return {'success': False, 'action': 'comparison_failed', 'error': str(e), ...}`. I grepped for the exact string and it is line 267, as cited. HTTP 200, no HTTPException, so the unified envelope never sees it. The contrast is verified: app/middleware/error_handler.py:131-162 ErrorHandlerMiddleware.dispatch replaces every unhandled exception with the constant `message='Internal server error'` plus a request_id. Route auth verified at image_routes.py:57-65 -- `user: Optional[Dict] = Depends(get_optional_user)` -- so an anonymous caller receives the raw exception text. P2 correct: a reconnaissance surface, not a direct compromise.

findings.title: npm audit --audit-level=high is NOT clean (1 critical, 20 high) and the CI job that would catch it is continue-on-error

findings.evidence: Raw run (this tree, 2026-08-31): `35 vulnerabilities (1 low, 13 moderate, 20 high, 1 critical)`. Critical: `tar` (node-tar PAX size override / parser confusion), transitive. HIGH with `isDirect=true`: `axios` ('Axios Node HTTP adapter can use an inherited proxy after interceptor config cloning'; 'Axios form serializer') pinned at `^1.13.4` in SmartCompareApp/package.json:20, and `expo` (~54.0.33). findings.title: Referral invite endpoints are unauthenticated, unrate-limited, and their path/query params are unvalidated
findings.claim: `GET /invite/{share_token}` and `POST /invite/{share_token}/quiz` use `get_optional_user` (so anonymous is fine by design), carry NO `@limiter.limit` decorator, and declare `share_token: str` and `ref: str` with no pattern or length bound - unlike the analogous share_routes token which is regex-pinned.
findings.evidence: app/api/referral_routes.py:248-253 - `async def resolve_invite(share_token: str, ref: str, user: Optional[dict] = Depends(get_optional_user))`; :275-280 same shape for the quiz POST. Neither has `@limiter.limit`, and per finding security-01 `default_limits` never apply. Contrast app/api/share_routes.py:56 which pins the token as `Path(..., pattern=r'^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{18,30}$')`. The quiz handler calls `service.run_invitee_quiz(...)` (referral_service) which resolves the invite and re-scores a stored comparison per request.
findings.failure_scenario: With `ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true` (flipped in Railway per CLAUDE.md), an anonymous client can hammer `POST /api/v1/referrals/invite/<anything>/quiz` at full speed - each call is a DB round-trip plus a re-score - with no limit and no auth. findings.fix_sketch: Add `@limiter.limit('20/minute')` (and `10/minute` on the quiz POST) and pin the params: `share_token: str = Path(..., pattern=r'^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{18,30}$')`, `ref: str = Query(..., pattern=r'^QR-[A-HJ-NP-Z2-9]{6}$')` - the invite-code alphabet is already defined at auth_routes.py:15.
findings.verify_evidence: app/api/referral_routes.py:248-253 `async def resolve_invite(share_token: str, ref: str, user: Optional[dict] = Depends(get_optional_user))` and :275-281 `async def submit_invitee_quiz(share_token: str, body: InviteeQuizRequest, user: ...)` -- read directly. No @limiter.limit above either (they are entries 15 and 16 on my own independently generated undecorated-route list), and no Path/Query pattern or length bound on share_token or ref. The contrast is real: app/api/share_routes.py:53-57 pins its token as `Path(..., pattern=r'^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{18,30}$')` AND carries `@limiter.limit('30/minute')`. Gating checked: CLAUDE.md:258 records ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM as 'default OFF in code, flipped in Railway', so this path IS live. P2 correct.

findings.title: Anonymous feedback/events writes use the service-role client with a client-supplied, unvalidated comparison_id
findings.claim: `save_feedback` and `track_events_batch` write through `get_supabase_client()` (the deprecated alias that returns the RLS-bypassing admin client) and attach whatever `comparison_id` the caller sent, with no ownership check and no UUID/length validation on the field.
findings.evidence: app/services/feedback_service.py:113 `client = get_supabase_client()` then :126 `client.table('comparison_feedback').insert(record)`; :145 and :174 the same for `user_events`. app/services/database_service.py:56-59 - `get_supabase_client()` is documented DEPRECATED and 'Returns admin client'. The value comes straight from app/api/feedback_routes.py:72 `comparison_id: Optional[str] = None` (no `Field(pattern=...)`, no max_length) and :91 the same on `EventItem`, both reached through `get_optional_user` so no auth is required at all.
findings.failure_scenario: An anonymous caller POSTs 50 events per request at 60 req/min, each pinned to another user's `comparison_id` harvested from a share link. The rows land under the service role (RLS cannot stop them) and poison `comparison_feedback` / `user_events` - the tables that feed the /admin/cohort dashboards, the pain-workflow derivation, and `save_comparison_and_track_cohort`. Nothing in the pipeline can distinguish the forged rows afterwards.
findings.fix_sketch: Validate `comparison_id` as a UUID at the Pydantic layer, and when the caller is authenticated write through `get_user_supabase_client(access_token)` so RLS applies. For anonymous writes, either drop `comparison_id` or verify the id resolves to a row with a live share_token before persisting.
findings.verify_evidence: app/services/feedback_service.py:113 `client = get_supabase_client()` then :126 `client.table('comparison_feedback').insert(record)`; :145 and :174 the same for user_events. app/services/database_service.py:56-60 confirms `get_supabase_client()` is docstringed DEPRECATED and does `return get_admin_supabase_client()`. comparison_id is attached unconditionally from the caller at :120-121 with no ownership check. app/api/feedback_routes.py:70-73 `comparison_id: Optional[str] = None` on FeedbackRequest and :90 on EventItem -- no pattern, no max_length -- both routes reached through get_optional_user. Mitigations the lane did not credit, and why this stays P2: event_type is whitelist-validated (:96-103), event_data is capped at 10KB (:89-94), MAX_BATCH_SIZE is 50 (:63), and both routes ARE rate limited (:119 30/minute, :148 60/minute). CORRECTION to the lane's fix_sketch, verified against migrations/010_enable_rls.sql:48-58: the INSERT policies are `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id OR user_id IS NULL)` and place NO constraint on comparison_id, so switching to get_user_supabase_client(access_token) would NOT stop the forgery. Only the UUID validation plus an ownership/share-token check actually fixes it. Claim CONFIRMED, remedy partly wrong.

findings.title: The admin static mount accepts the admin key over HTTP Basic with no rate limit, so key-guessing is unbounded
findings.claim: `_AdminAuthenticatedStaticFiles` validates the same `ADMIN_API_KEY` that `/api/v1/admin/*` protects, but the mount is an ASGI app outside the router layer, so none of slowapi's decorators apply and (per security-01) no default limit exists either - guessing attempts against /admin/*.html are unthrottled while the JSON endpoints are 30/minute.
findings.evidence: app/main.py:165-219 - the StaticFiles subclass compares `X-Admin-Key` (:191) or the HTTP Basic password (:195-204) against `os.getenv('ADMIN_API_KEY')` with `hmac.compare_digest`, then `app.mount('/admin', ...)`. There is no limiter involvement anywhere in the class, and the mount is registered directly on `app`. app/api/admin_routes.py:43 shows the JSON side does carry `@limiter.limit('30/minute')`.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker points a Basic-auth brute-forcer at `https://<host>/admin/costs.html`. If ADMIN_API_KEY is anything short of high-entropy (it is an operator-chosen env var, not a generated one), the attempt rate is bounded only by network throughput. A success yields the service-role-backed analytics surface AND the working key for all 19 /api/v1/admin/* endpoints, including `/audit-log` (raw security events with user ids).
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the mount in a small ASGI throttle keyed on the peer/XFF, or move the static gate behind a router-level dependency so `@limiter.limit` applies. Independently, generate ADMIN_API_KEY as 32+ random bytes and document the rotation like the Serper playbook.
findings.verify_evidence: app/main.py:165-219 read in full. `_AdminAuthenticatedStaticFiles.__call__` compares x-admin-key at :191 and the HTTP Basic password at :200 against `os.getenv('ADMIN_API_KEY')` with `_hmac.compare_digest`, returning 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Qaren Admin"` on a miss. findings.title: Prompt-injection detection only logs; the documented injection_attempt audit event is never emitted, and the raw query is logged

findings.evidence: app/services/extraction_service.py:1312-1315: `sanitized_query = sanitize_prompt_input(query, max_length=500)` then `if check_injection_patterns(query): logger.warning(...)` - no branch, no raise, no audit call. `grep -rn 'check_injection_patterns' app/` returns exactly two hits: the import at extraction_service.py:20 and this call. app/services/audit_service.py exposes `log_audit_event` (whose docstring at :26 lists `injection_attempt` as a valid event_type) and `log_content_blocked` - neither is called from any injection site. Decide explicitly whether detection should also block - today it is detect-and-continue with no record.

No branch, no raise, no audit call. The only other hits are the import at :20, the definition at app/utils/prompt_sanitizer.py:41, and 11 assertions in tests/test_prompt_injection.py. `grep -rn injection_attempt app/ --include=*.py` returns exactly ONE hit -- the docstring listing at audit_service.py:26 -- so no code path ever writes that event_type, while CLAUDE.md:163 advertises it. findings.title: CORS defaults ship localhost origins with allow_credentials=True, and CORS_ORIGINS='*' would be accepted
findings.claim: `_DEFAULT_ORIGINS` includes three `http://localhost:*` entries and is used verbatim in production whenever `CORS_ORIGINS` is unset, with `allow_credentials=True`; and `_get_allowed_origins` performs no validation, so setting `CORS_ORIGINS=*` would be honoured.
findings.evidence: app/main.py:86-107 - `_DEFAULT_ORIGINS = ['https://web-production-58776.up.railway.app', 'http://localhost:8000', 'http://localhost:19006', 'http://localhost:8081']`; `_get_allowed_origins()` splits `CORS_ORIGINS` on commas with no allowlist or wildcard rejection; `app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS, allow_credentials=True, ...)`. CLAUDE.md lists `CORS_ORIGINS` as Optional, so the default path is the live path unless someone set it.
findings.failure_scenario: Any page a victim can be induced to load from `http://localhost:8081` or `http://localhost:19006` (a locally running dev server, a malicious Electron/desktop app, a compromised local tool) gets credentialed cross-origin access to the production API. And a future operator setting `CORS_ORIGINS=*` to 'fix' a CORS error silently converts the API to origin-reflection-with-credentials, since Starlette's CORSMiddleware pairs `allow_origin_regex`-free `['*']` with credentials by echoing the request Origin.
findings.fix_sketch: Split the defaults: production defaults to the Railway origin only; the localhost entries are added only when `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT` is unset. Reject `*` in `_get_allowed_origins` when `allow_credentials=True` (raise at startup rather than degrade silently).
findings.verify_evidence: Code facts exact: app/main.py:86-91 `_DEFAULT_ORIGINS` is the Railway origin plus http://localhost:8000, :19006 and :8081; :93-99 `_get_allowed_origins` splits CORS_ORIGINS on commas with no allowlist and no wildcard rejection; :101-107 `add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS, allow_credentials=True, ...)`. I checked the wildcard sub-claim against the INSTALLED starlette rather than from memory: `preflight_explicit_allow_origin = not allow_all_origins or allow_credentials`, so with '*' plus credentials the PREFLIGHT does echo the specific origin, as claimed. But the non-preflight path sets `simple_headers['Access-Control-Allow-Origin'] = '*'` and swaps in the explicit origin only `if self.allow_all_origins and has_cookie`. This API authenticates with a Bearer header and uses no cookies, so 'credentialed cross-origin access' overstates the impact: an attacker's page still needs the victim's token, which CORS does not hand over. KNOWN_ITEM CORRECTION (the lane had known_item:false): docs/CONTEXT_DECISIONS_BUGS.md:43 records 'CORS restricted origins | Only Railway + localhost, not wildcard ["*"]' as a DELIBERATE decision that the code matches. The status claim is not wrong, so under the review's own ground rules the reportable value here is near zero. P3, known_item true.
findings.known_item_correction: Lane had known_item:false. docs/CONTEXT_DECISIONS_BUGS.md:43 documents 'CORS restricted origins | Only Railway + localhost, not wildcard ["*"]' as a deliberate decision that the code matches.

findings.title: verify_admin_key 500s instead of 403 on a non-ASCII X-Admin-Key
findings.claim: `hmac.compare_digest(x_admin_key, expected)` on two `str` arguments raises `TypeError` when either contains a non-ASCII codepoint, so a header like `X-Admin-Key: \u00e9` produces an unhandled exception rather than the intended 403.
findings.evidence: app/api/admin_routes.py:34-39: `def verify_admin_key(x_admin_key: str = Header(...)): expected = os.getenv('ADMIN_API_KEY', ''); if not expected or not hmac.compare_digest(x_admin_key, expected): raise HTTPException(403, ...)`. CPython's `hmac.compare_digest` requires both str operands to be ASCII-only and raises `TypeError: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported`. The same construct in app/main.py:191/:200 (the static mount) has the identical exposure; app/api/history_routes.py:150/:188 compares UUID strings so it is safe.
findings.failure_scenario: `curl -H 'X-Admin-Key: \u00e9' https://<host>/api/v1/admin/costs` returns a 500 with `code: SERVER_ERROR` and fires `sentry_sdk.capture_exception` (error_handler.py:152), turning a trivially-sendable header into a Sentry-noise generator and a 403-vs-500 oracle. Not a bypass - the failure is closed - but it is an unauthenticated path to a 500.
findings.fix_sketch: Compare bytes: `hmac.compare_digest(x_admin_key.encode('utf-8'), expected.encode('utf-8'))`, in admin_routes.py and both sites in main.py.
findings.verify_evidence: app/api/admin_routes.py:34-39 read directly: `def verify_admin_key(x_admin_key: str = Header(...)): expected = os.getenv('ADMIN_API_KEY', ''); if not expected or not hmac.compare_digest(x_admin_key, expected): raise HTTPException(status_code=403, ...)` -- two str operands, at line 37. RAN a zero-network repro against this tree's real dependencies (ADMIN_API_KEY='testsecret', the route behind Depends(verify_admin_key), wrapped in the repo's own ErrorHandlerMiddleware): a wrong ASCII key returns 403; a raw `\xe9` header byte, which Starlette decodes latin-1 into a non-ASCII str, raises `TypeError: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported` at admin_routes.py:37 and the middleware returns `500 {"success":false,"error":"Internal server error","code":"SERVER_ERROR"}`. Exactly the claimed 403-vs-500 oracle plus a capture_exception. Worth noting the httpx client itself refuses to SEND such a header, so this needs a raw client such as curl, not a browser or the app. The same construct at main.py:191/:200 has the identical exposure. Fails closed, so P3 is right.

findings.title: .claude/settings.local.json is committed with a blanket Bash allowlist every clone inherits
findings.claim: The per-machine agent settings file is tracked in git and grants unconditional `Bash(python:*)`, `Bash(curl:*)`, `Bash(pip install:*)`, `Bash(npm install:*)` and `Bash(git push:*)`, so any clone or worktree of this repo starts with those approvals already in place.
findings.evidence: `.claude/settings.local.json` is present in the pinned tree (it is not in .gitignore, whose agent-scratch entries are `.qa-*/`, `.agents/`, `.codex/`). Its `permissions.allow` array contains `"Bash(python:*)"`, `"Bash(curl:*)"`, `"Bash(pip install:*)"`, `"Bash(npm install:*)"`, `"Bash(git push:*)"` and `"Bash(git commit:*)"` alongside Supabase MCP write tools (`mcp__plugin_supabase_supabase__apply_migration`, `execute_sql`).
findings.failure_scenario: `Bash(python:*)` plus `Bash(curl:*)` is a full arbitrary-execution grant - an agent following a poisoned instruction found in scraped page content, a fixture, or a doc can run any command without a prompt, and `Bash(git push:*)` lets the result reach main. The whole point of the `.local.json` suffix is that it stays per-machine; committing it makes one operator's accumulated trust decisions the default for everyone who clones.
findings.fix_sketch: `git rm --cached .claude/settings.local.json` and add `.claude/settings.local.json` to .gitignore (keep the shared `.claude/settings.json`). Re-grant per machine, and narrow `Bash(python:*)`/`Bash(curl:*)` to the specific invocations that were actually needed.
findings.verify_evidence: `git ls-files .claude/` in this tree returns `.claude/settings.json` AND `.claude/settings.local.json` -- the per-machine file IS tracked, exactly as claimed, and it is absent from .gitignore. I read its permissions.allow array myself: it contains `Bash(python:*)`, `Bash(curl:*)`, `Bash(pip install:*)`, `Bash(npm install:*)`, `Bash(npx expo *)`, `Bash(git push:*)`, `Bash(git commit:*)`, `Bash(timeout:*)`, `WebSearch`, plus `mcp__plugin_supabase_supabase__apply_migration` and `mcp__plugin_supabase_supabase__execute_sql` -- migration and raw-SQL write tools. Several entries even embed another machine's absolute Windows paths, which is the clearest proof the file is machine-scoped. `Bash(python:*)` plus `Bash(curl:*)` together is an unconditional arbitrary-execution grant that every clone and worktree inherits. P3 correct: agent-session hygiene, not a runtime application vulnerability.

findings.title: Admin /costs runs an unbounded month-wide select, so the number is silently truncated and the endpoint is a memory risk
findings.claim: `api_costs` selects every `comparisons.metadata` row since the start of the month with no `.limit()` and no pagination, then sums in Python - PostgREST silently caps the response, so the reported OpenAI cost is wrong once the month exceeds that cap.
findings.evidence: app/api/admin_routes.py:107-113: `supabase.table('comparisons').select('metadata').gte('created_at', month_start).execute()` then `for row in (result.data or []): openai_cost += meta.get('total_cost', 0)`. No `.limit()`, no `.range()`. The count query immediately below (:122) correctly uses `count='exact'` and does not fetch rows, which makes the mismatch visible: `comparisons_this_month` will keep climbing while `openai.cost_usd` plateaus.
findings.failure_scenario: Once a month exceeds PostgREST's default max-rows, `summary['openai']['cost_usd']` and therefore `avg_cost_per_comparison` and `estimated_monthly_total` are all understated, with no error and no warning - the cost dashboard that CLAUDE.md points at for spend decisions quietly reports a floor instead of a total. Before that cap, pulling every metadata JSONB blob for a month into the dyno is also a needless memory spike on a 30/minute endpoint.
findings.fix_sketch: Do the sum in Postgres - an RPC or a view returning `sum((metadata->>'total_cost')::numeric)` for the window - or page with `.range()` until exhausted. Assert in a test that the returned cost is consistent with `comparisons_this_month` at row counts above the PostgREST cap.
findings.verify_evidence: app/api/admin_routes.py:107-113 read directly: `supabase.table('comparisons').select('metadata').gte('created_at', month_start).execute()` followed by a Python `for row in (result.data or []): openai_cost += meta.get('total_cost', 0)`. No .limit(), no .range(). The count query at :119-124 does use `count='exact'`, so the two numbers diverge silently exactly as described once the month exceeds PostgREST's max-rows (Supabase ships a 1000-row default). PARTIAL REFUTATION of the finding's own second half: it argues BOTH that 'PostgREST silently caps the response' AND that 'pulling every metadata JSONB blob for a month into the dyno is a memory spike'. Those are mutually exclusive -- the very cap that causes the silent truncation is what prevents the memory spike. The truncation / under-reporting claim stands; the memory-risk half of the title does not. Also note this is a correctness/availability finding, not a security one -- the weakest fit for this lane. P3.
